name: Etna fissure eruption, Italy

signal.label: Radar coherence across the event
signal.positive: 1 = the surface looks the same in both passes
signal.noise_method: robust scatter of differences between neighbouring cells (includes real gradients)

line.name: the edge of the new lava
line.raster_unit: coherence lost, 0 to 1 (a copy of cohdrop.u8)
line.measured_means: a patch where coherence loss reaches 0.5: the radar clearly stopped matching itself there
line.dashed_means: a patch of coherence loss above 0.35 that never reaches 0.5: possible lava, possible noise
line.caveat: Coherence loss is not lava: snow, ash, vegetation and steep slopes also break the match. The outline is the 0.35 contour of the coherence loss (lightly smoothed), kept only for patches of 25 cells or more within 2.5 km of the three stories that sit on the new lava. Dropped: the radial streaks on the north-east and south flanks, which follow gullies and are not tied to any story. The outline covers the vent area at Monte Rittmann and the flow's upper reach (about 4.4 km long, loss up to 0.8) but does not reach the lava-front story: the faint tongue toward it (a few cells, about 400 m wide, loss only 0.2 to 0.4) is below the 0.35 contour, so that story is off the line by about 1.4 km.
